questions.question: An element 'X' forms an oxide with the formula X2O3. To which group of the periodic table does 'X' belong?
questions.solution: (c) Group 13. In X2O3 the valency of X is 3, so X has 3 valence electrons and belongs to Group 13 (e.g. Al2O3).

questions.question:
In the reaction given below concentrated sulphuric acid acts as an:
S + 2H2SO4 (conc) → 3SO2 + 2H2O
questions.solution: (c) Oxidising agent. Conc. H2SO4 oxidises sulphur to SO2 and is itself reduced to SO2.

questions.question: Which one of the following would weigh the least? [At. wt. Ag = 108, N = 14, O = 16, C = 12]

options.c: 22.4 litres of oxygen gas at STP

questions.solution: (d) 6.023 × 10^23 atoms of carbon = 1 mole C = 12 g. Others: 2 gram atoms N = 28 g; 1 mole Ag = 108 g; 22.4 L O2 at STP = 32 g.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an incorrect statement?

options.b: The subsequent members of a homologous series differ by a -CH group
options.d: The members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties

questions.solution: (b) Incorrect: successive members of a homologous series differ by a -CH2- group, not -CH.

questions.topic: Action of NH4OH on salt solutions
questions.question: A nitrate which forms a precipitate with ammonium hydroxide and is also soluble in excess of it:
questions.solution: (d) Copper nitrate. It gives a pale blue precipitate of Cu(OH)2 which dissolves in excess NH4OH forming a deep (inky) blue solution of [Cu(NH3)4]SO4-type complex; Fe(OH)2, Fe(OH)3 and Pb(OH)2 are insoluble in excess.

concepts: n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass
questions.question: If the empirical formula mass of the formula PQ2 is 10 and the relative molecular mass is 30, then the molecular formula will be ______.
questions.solution: (d) P3Q6. n = 30/10 = 3, so molecular formula = (PQ2)3 = P3Q6.

questions.question:
Which apparatus could be used to electroplate an iron nail with copper? (Key: rectangle = copper sheet; nail symbol = iron nail.)
L: iron nail connected to + terminal, copper sheet to − terminal, in aqueous iron(II) sulphate.
M: copper sheet connected to + terminal, iron nail to − terminal, in aqueous iron(II) sulphate.
N: iron nail connected to + terminal, copper sheet to − terminal, in aqueous copper(II) sulphate.
O: copper sheet connected to + terminal, iron nail to − terminal, in aqueous copper(II) sulphate.
questions.solution: (d) O. For copper plating, the iron nail (article) must be the cathode (−), the copper sheet the anode (+), and the electrolyte must contain Cu2+ ions (aqueous copper(II) sulphate).
questions.figure_desc: Four electrolytic cells L, M, N, O showing iron nail and copper sheet connected to + / − terminals in iron(II) sulphate or copper(II) sulphate solution.

concepts: covalent non-polar compounds do not ionise
questions.question:
Which of the following compounds neither dissociate nor ionise in water?
A. Hydrochloric acid
B. Methane
C. Potassium nitrate
D. Carbon tetrachloride
questions.solution: (c) Both B and D. Methane and carbon tetrachloride are non-polar covalent compounds; HCl ionises and KNO3 dissociates in water.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Chlorine forms a stable ion with the same electronic configuration as argon.
Reason (R): Chlorine has seven valence electrons and to complete its octet, it gains one electron.

options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: (c) Both true and R explains A: Cl (2,8,7) gains one electron to form Cl⁻ (2,8,8), the configuration of argon.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Dry hydrogen chloride gas is collected by the upward displacement of air.
Reason (R): Hydrogen chloride gas is lighter than air.

options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: (a) A is true, R is false. HCl (VD 18.25) is heavier than air (VD 14.4), so it is collected by upward displacement of air.

concepts: oxidation of non-metals by conc. HNO3
questions.question: Choose the correct set of products formed when concentrated nitric acid reacts with sulphur:
questions.solution: (a) H2SO4, H2O, NO2. S + 6HNO3 (conc) → H2SO4 + 6NO2 + 2H2O.

questions.question: The method in which separation of the ore and gangue takes place by preferential wetting process is:
questions.solution: (c) Froth flotation: ore particles are preferentially wetted by oil and gangue by water.

concepts: triple bond needs two addition steps
questions.question:
Which of the following chains of hydrocarbons undergoes two steps of reactions to become saturated?
(a) –C–C– (single bond)
(b) –C=C– (double bond)
(c) –C≡C– (triple bond)
(d) a three-membered carbon ring (cyclic, all single bonds)

options.d: three-membered carbon ring with single bonds

questions.solution: (c) –C≡C–. A triple bond adds two molecules (e.g. H2) in two steps: C≡C → C=C → C–C.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Which of the following observations correctly shows the action of indicators on potassium hydroxide solution?
Indicator | Phenolphthalein | Methyl orange
1 | pink to colourless | remains orange
2 | colourless to pink | orange to yellow
3 | remains pink | orange to pink
4 | remains colourless | orange to yellow
questions.solution: (b) 2. In KOH (alkali), phenolphthalein turns from colourless to pink and methyl orange from orange to yellow.

questions.question: Which reaction gives copper as one of the products?

options.b: Passing dry ammonia gas over heated copper oxide.
options.c: Passing oxygen gas over heated copper oxide.
options.d: Silver coin dropped in copper sulphate solution

questions.solution: (b) 3CuO + 2NH3 → 3Cu + 3H2O + N2. Ammonia reduces copper oxide to copper.

questions.question:
The figure given below illustrates the apparatus used in the laboratory preparation of ammonia (round bottom flask containing sal ammoniac + slaked lime heated in an inclined position; gas passed through drying tower 'Y' and collected by downward displacement of air). With respect to this, answer the following questions:
(a) Write a balanced chemical equation for the laboratory preparation of ammonia.
(b) Why is slaked lime preferred in the above preparation?
(c) Name the drying agent 'Y' used in the above process.
(d) Why is the round bottom flask kept at an inclined position?
(e) State one identification test for ammonia gas.
questions.solution:
(a) 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 → CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3↑
(b) Slaked lime is cheap and not deliquescent; it gives a controlled reaction (NaOH/KOH are costly and deliquescent).
(c) Quicklime (CaO).
(d) So that the water formed in the reaction does not trickle back onto the hot part of the flask and crack it.
(e) A glass rod dipped in conc. HCl brought near the gas gives dense white fumes of NH4Cl (or ammonia turns moist red litmus blue).

marking_points.point: Prevent water trickling back and cracking flask
Dense white fumes with conc. HCl rod / moist red litmus blue

questions.figure_desc: Laboratory set-up for ammonia: inclined flask with sal ammoniac + slaked lime heated, gas through drying tower Y, collected in inverted jar.

questions.question:
Identify the following:
(a) Organic compounds having the same molecular formula but differ in the structural formula.
(b) The energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous isolated atom to form a negatively charged ion.
(c) The process of formation of ions from molecules which are not in the ionic state.
(d) The process by which certain ores, especially carbonates, are converted to oxides in the absence of air.
(e) The ratio of the mass of a certain volume of gas to the mass of the same volume of hydrogen measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.

answer_items.prompt: Same molecular formula, different structural formula
Energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom
Formation of ions from molecules not in the ionic state
Ores (carbonates) converted to oxides in absence of air
Ratio of mass of a volume of gas to same volume of hydrogen

questions.solution:
(a) Isomers
(b) Electron affinity
(c) Ionisation
(d) Calcination
(e) Vapour density

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Complete the following by choosing the correct answers from the brackets:
(a) During the electrolysis of copper sulphate solution, if ______ is used as an electrode, the colour of the electrolyte does not fade. (platinum/copper)
(b) Ammonia reacts with excess chlorine to form ______ (nitrogen trichloride/ammonium chloride).
(c) ______ solution forms a white precipitate with sodium hydroxide solution and insoluble in excess of it. (zinc chloride/calcium chloride)
(d) The salt formed when ZnO reacts with hot concentrated NaOH is ______ (zinc hydroxide/sodium zincate)
(e) Magnesium reacts with very dilute nitric acid to liberate ______ (H2/NO2)

answer_items.prompt: Electrode for which CuSO4 colour does not fade
White ppt with NaOH insoluble in excess
Salt from ZnO + hot conc. NaOH
Gas from Mg + very dilute HNO3

questions.solution:
(a) copper
(b) nitrogen trichloride
(c) calcium chloride
(d) sodium zincate
(e) H2

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Match the salts given in Column A with their method of preparation given in Column B:
Column A: (a) FeCl3 from Fe  (b) ZnSO4 from Zn  (c) CuSO4 from CuO  (d) Na2SO4 from NaOH  (e) CaCO3 from CaCl2
Column B: 1. Titration  2. Combination  3. Simple Displacement  4. Precipitation  5. Neutralisation
questions.solution:
(a) FeCl3 from Fe – 2. Combination (2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3)
(b) ZnSO4 from Zn – 3. Simple displacement (Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2)
(c) CuSO4 from CuO – 5. Neutralisation (CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O)
(d) Na2SO4 from NaOH – 1. Titration (2NaOH + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O)
(e) CaCO3 from CaCl2 – 4. Precipitation (CaCl2 + Na2CO3 → CaCO3↓ + 2NaCl)

questions.question:
(a) Give the IUPAC name of the following organic compounds:
1. H2C=CH2 (two carbons joined by a double bond, each carrying two H atoms)
2. CH3–CH(CH3)–CH2–COOH (a four-carbon chain ending in –COOH, with a –CH3 branch on the third carbon from the COOH end)
(b) Draw the structural diagrams for the following compounds:
1. 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane
2. 2-butanol
3. Propanal
questions.solution:
(a) 1. Ethene
2. 3-Methylbutanoic acid
(b) 1. 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane: Cl2CH–CHCl2 (two C atoms single-bonded; each C carries two Cl and one H).
2. 2-butanol: CH3–CH(OH)–CH2–CH3 (four-carbon chain with –OH on C2; all other valencies H).
3. Propanal: CH3–CH2–CHO (three-carbon chain, C1 is –C(=O)H).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Radha was performing a test for a specific radical. During this test, she performed the following steps:
Step 1: Dilute nitric acid was taken in a test tube which was mixed with a freshly prepared solution of iron(II) sulphate.
Step 2: Conc. H2SO4 was poured carefully from the sides of the test tube taken in step 1. The test tube was set aside for a few minutes.
Answer the following questions based on the above experiment.
(a) What will Radha observe after the completion of the above experiment?
(b) Why did Radha choose freshly prepared iron(II) sulphate solution in the above experiment?
(c) Identify the specific radical that was tested in this experiment.
questions.solution:
(a) A brown ring forms at the junction of the two liquids (due to FeSO4·NO).
(b) Iron(II) sulphate solution is oxidised by air to iron(III) sulphate on standing; only Fe2+ forms the brown nitroso-ferrous sulphate complex, so it must be freshly prepared.
(c) Nitrate ion (NO3⁻).

marking_points.point: Brown ring at junction of liquids
Fresh FeSO4 because it gets oxidised to ferric salt on standing

questions.question:
Arrange the following as per the instructions given in the brackets:
(a) Mg, Cl, Na, S, Si (increasing order of atomic size).
(b) B, Be, N, Li, C, O (decreasing order of ionisation potential)
questions.solution:
(a) Cl < S < Si < Mg < Na
(b) O > N > C > B > Be > Li (general trend: ionisation potential increases across a period). Note: actual data give N > O > C > Be > B > Li because of the stable half-filled/filled subshells, but the ICSE expected answer follows the general trend.

Aluminium is a lightweight, strong and versatile metal whose extraction is important to a wide range of industries from aircrafts to kitchenware. With respect to the extraction of aluminium from bauxite ore, answer the following questions:

concepts: BaSO4 white ppt insoluble in HCl
questions.question:
Priya was given an unknown salt 'D' for identification. She prepared a solution of the salt 'D' and divided it into two parts. To the first part of the salt solution, she added a few drops of sodium hydroxide solution and obtained a dirty green precipitate. To the second part of the salt solution, she added a few drops of barium chloride solution and obtained a white precipitate insoluble in excess of dilute HCl.
Identify the cation and the anion present in the salt 'D' given to Priya for identification.
questions.solution:
Cation: iron(II) / ferrous ion, Fe2+ (dirty green Fe(OH)2).
Anion: sulphate ion, SO4 2- (white BaSO4 insoluble in dil. HCl). Salt D is FeSO4.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The following questions are pertaining to the laboratory preparation of hydrogen chloride gas:
(a) Write the equation for its preparation with the necessary conditions.
(b) Name the drying agent used and justify your choice.
(c) State a safety precaution you would take during the preparation of hydrochloric acid.
questions.solution:
(a) NaCl + H2SO4 (conc) → NaHSO4 + HCl↑ (temperature below 200°C)
(b) Concentrated sulphuric acid; it does not react with HCl, whereas other drying agents like CaO and P2O5 react with it.
(c) Use the inverted funnel arrangement (rim just touching the water surface) when dissolving HCl in water, to prevent back suction.

marking_points.point: Conc. H2SO4, does not react with HCl
Funnel arrangement to prevent back suction

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Naman took two different salt solutions in test tubes 'X' (AgNO3 solution) and 'Y' (Pb(NO3)2 solution) as shown in the figure. He added dilute HCl to each of the two test tubes. The products formed in the test tubes P and Q are silver chloride and lead chloride respectively.
State:
(a) One common observation made by Naman in both the reactions.
(b) The observation made by him on addition of excess of ammonium hydroxide to the products formed in:
(1) Test tube X
(2) Test tube Y
questions.solution:
(a) A white precipitate forms in both test tubes (AgCl and PbCl2).
(b)(1) X: the white precipitate of AgCl dissolves in excess NH4OH forming a clear, colourless solution (diammine silver complex).
(2) Y: the white precipitate of PbCl2 remains insoluble in excess NH4OH.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Solid sodium bicarbonate decomposes as follows:
2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O
If 168 grams of sodium bicarbonate decomposes, calculate:
(a) the number of moles of sodium bicarbonate decomposed.
(b) the mass of sodium carbonate formed.
[At. wt. Na = 23, H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.solution:
(a) Molar mass NaHCO3 = 23 + 1 + 12 + 48 = 84 g/mol. Moles = 168/84 = 2 mol.
(b) 2 mol NaHCO3 give 1 mol Na2CO3. Molar mass Na2CO3 = 46 + 12 + 48 = 106 g. Mass formed = 106 g.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Draw the electron dot diagrams for each of the following:
(a) An ionic compound formed when Mg reacts with dilute HCl.
(b) The formation of a hydronium ion.
[Atomic no. Mg = 12, H = 1, Cl = 17, O = 8]
questions.solution:
(a) MgCl2: Mg (2,8,2) transfers one electron to each of two Cl atoms (2,8,7), giving Mg2+ and 2[:Cl:]⁻ each with a complete octet: [Cl]⁻ [Mg]2+ [Cl]⁻ with 8 dots/crosses around each Cl.
(b) H2O has two lone pairs on O; one lone pair is donated to H⁺ forming a coordinate bond: H2O + H⁺ → [H3O]⁺, O with 3 bonded pairs (2 covalent + 1 coordinate) and one lone pair.

marking_points.point: Electron transfer Mg to 2 Cl shown
Coordinate bond to H+ forming H3O+ with charge

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Reasons - covalent compounds and Contact process
questions.question:
Give reasons:
(i) Covalent compounds have a low melting and boiling point.
(ii) In the Contact process, sulphur trioxide vapours are not absorbed in water.
questions.solution:
(i) Covalent compounds consist of molecules held by weak intermolecular (van der Waals) forces, so little energy is needed to separate them.
(ii) SO3 reacts with water very exothermically, forming a dense fog of sulphuric acid droplets that does not condense easily; hence SO3 is absorbed in conc. H2SO4 to form oleum instead.

marking_points.point: Highly exothermic, forms dense acid mist/fog

(b) Oxidising agent: Cu + 2H2SO4 → CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O
(c) Dehydrating agent: C2H5OH → C2H4 + H2O (conc. H2SO4, 170°C)

questions.question:
State one significant observation in each of the following:

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With respect to the Hall Heroult's process related to the extraction of aluminium, answer the following questions:
(a) Why is powdered coke sprinkled over the electrolytic mixture undergoing electrolytic reduction?
(b) Why are graphite anodes continuously replaced during the electrolysis?
(c) Write the equation for the formation of aluminium at the cathode.
questions.solution:
(a) To reduce heat loss by radiation from the surface and to prevent the burning (oxidation) of the anode in air.
(b) Oxygen liberated at the anode reacts with the carbon anode forming CO2/CO, so the anodes are gradually consumed.
(c) Al3+ + 3e⁻ → Al

marking_points.point: Reduces heat loss / prevents anode burning
Anodes oxidised by O2 to CO2

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: If 6 litres of hydrogen and 4 litres of chlorine are mixed and exploded and if water is added to the gases formed, calculate the volume of the residual gas.
questions.solution:
H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl (1 vol : 1 vol : 2 vol).
4 L Cl2 reacts with 4 L H2 to form 8 L HCl; 6 − 4 = 2 L H2 remains unreacted.
On adding water, the 8 L HCl dissolves. Residual gas = 2 litres of hydrogen.

marking_points.point: Volume ratio applied: 4 L H2 reacts with 4 L Cl2, forming 8 L HCl

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Lead bromide, an inorganic white powder is generally produced in the burning of typical leaded gasoline. If lead bromide undergoes electrolysis process in the molten state, then answer the following questions:
(a) Write the equation for the reaction taking place at the cathode.
(b) Why are graphite anodes preferred in the above electrolysis?
(c) What would happen if solid lead bromide is used in the above electrolysis?
questions.solution:
(a) Pb2+ + 2e⁻ → Pb
(b) Graphite is inert and is not attacked by the reactive bromine vapours liberated at the anode.
(c) No electrolysis occurs: in the solid state the Pb2+ and Br⁻ ions are held in a rigid lattice and are not free to move, so solid PbBr2 does not conduct electricity.

marking_points.point: Graphite inert / not attacked by bromine
No conduction; ions not free in solid

questions.question:
From the given list of compounds, select the one that fits the description given below:
Iron, sodium hydroxide, hydrochloric acid, molybdenum, lead hydroxide, sulphuric acid
(a) This acid cannot form an acid salt.
(b) The promoter used in Haber's process.

answer_items.prompt: Acid that cannot form an acid salt
Base which is not an alkali

questions.solution:
(a) Hydrochloric acid (monobasic)
(b) Molybdenum
(c) Lead hydroxide (insoluble in water)
